# No grading system for recruiting agencies yet

Speakers call for accountability, migrant protection

Published : 29 October 2026

•

Updated : 29 October 2026, 08:53

• [BANGLADESH](/news/bangladesh)

SHARE ![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

[![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)](https://x.com/intent/tweet?text=No%20grading%20system%20for%20recruiting%20agencies%20yet&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.thedailystar.net%2Fnews%2Fbangladesh%2Fnews%2Fno-grading-system-recruiting-agencies-yet-4310151) [![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)](https://www.facebook.com/sharer/sharer.php?u=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.thedailystar.net%2Fnews%2Fbangladesh%2Fnews%2Fno-grading-system-recruiting-agencies-yet-4310151) [![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)](https://www.linkedin.com/shareArticle?mini=true&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.thedailystar.net%2Fnews%2Fbangladesh%2Fnews%2Fno-grading-system-recruiting-agencies-yet-4310151&title=No%20grading%20system%20for%20recruiting%20agencies%20yet)

![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

Staff Correspondent

![Migration_Dialogue.jpg](/sites/default/files/styles/big_1/public/2026-10/Migration_Dialogue.jpg?h=4521fff0)

Photo: Courtesy

The government has yet to introduce an effective grading system for recruiting agencies, leaving prospective migrant workers without an official way to assess recruiters before paying for overseas jobs.

State Minister for Expatriates’ Welfare and Overseas Employment Nurul Haque Nur acknowledged the shortcoming yesterday at a dialogue titled “Fair and Ethical Recruitment: Accountable Sub-agents”. 

[Tap here to add The Daily Star as a trusted source ![google-preferred-source-badge](/themes/custom/swallow/images/google_preferred_source_badge_dark.webp)](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=thedailystar.net)

Supported by The Asia Foundation and funded by FCDO, the event was organised by Witness Foundation at a Dhaka hotel.

> ![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)
>
> ## Workers often lacked receipts or other payment evidence, making complaints against intermediaries difficult to pursue.
>
> Pervez Siddiqui Director of Witness Foundation Executive

Nur said he could not confidently recommend a recruiting agency even to people from his own constituency seeking jobs abroad. Although the issue had been discussed with the prime minister, little progress had been made, he said.

He added that the software for recruiting agencies to submit details of their sub-agents was not fully operational. Agencies would eventually have to submit lists of their representatives for publication on the ministry’s website so workers could verify their identities before making payments.

He also questioned whether existing training courses matched overseas job demand and whether training centres tracked how many trainees secured jobs abroad.

Presenting data, Witness Foundation Executive Director Pervez Siddiqui said overseas employment fell 32 percent to 5,69,979 workers during January-September this year, from 8,38,892 in the same period last year, although remittances reached \$35.56 billion in FY2025-26.

Migrants needed around 14 months to recover their recruitment expenses, he said.

Of 1,414 complaints, 785 had been resolved, with Tk 6.48 crore refunded to affected workers, he said. Workers often lacked receipts or other payment evidence, making complaints against intermediaries difficult to pursue.

Syed Saiful Haque, chairperson of WARBE Development Foundation, alleged that agencies collected large sums without receipts, while intermediaries obscured accountability. He also accused many agencies of trading visas.

Advocate Farida Yeasmin of the Centre for Women and Children Studies said legal recognition of sub-agents would achieve little without enforcement. Referring to the 2023 legal amendment and 2025 regulations, she called for updated lists of registered intermediaries and proposed using the BMET digital system to monitor compliance.

ILO National Programme Manager Rehnuma Salam Khan urged the government to assess workers’ skills, working conditions and protection, as well as whether migrant complaints were declining.

Fakhrul Islam, a former joint secretary of the Bangladesh Association of International Recruiting Agencies (BAIRA), proposed online recruitment records listing selected workers and authorised charges, with payments through banks and legal action against agencies that overcharged.

Former BAIRA secretary-general Ali Haider Chowdhury called for diversifying labour markets, providing demand-based training and punishing trafficking networks.

Former expatriates’ welfare secretary Kazi Abul Kalam, expatriates’ welfare ministry Additional Secretary Ahmadul Haque, and Ahmed Aziz of the International Organization for Migration also spoke.
